clue.text: Gift from 9 15, much ridiculed affair with Eze, Pepi and Cunha at first confused

indicators.note: the listed letters are muddled up, so confused signals they must be rearranged
at first asks for only the opening letter of the footballer's name Cunha

explanation.surface: A footballing scene: some much-mocked affair involving the players Eze, Pepi and Cunha ends in confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 and 15 together are GIANNI INFANTINO, the FIFA president, who in 2025 gave Donald Trump a newly invented peace award that was widely mocked. 'confused' shuffles AFFAIR, EZE, PEPI and C.
explanation.definitionFit: The award was created and handed over by FIFA's head, and its presentation drew widespread derision.

clue.text: Flawed statement from 4?

definitions.meaning: flawed means having faults, not whole or complete
an egotist at 4 might announce '...', which is how the letters split as a spoken claim

explanation.surface: A faulty remark made by the person at 4 down.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the letters as I'M PERFECT and you have exactly what an egomaniac would say about himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with defects falls short of completeness, the ordinary sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Kneecap nearly (but not totally) something that makes you feel unwell

definitions.text: something that makes you feel unwell

indicators.note: only part of the two words is used, so the letters needed sit inside them

explanation.surface: A knee injury that nearly, though not quite, leaves you feeling ill.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the join of kneeCAP NEArly. APNEA is the American spelling of apnoea.
explanation.definitionFit: Apnoea, interrupted breathing during sleep, is a condition that leaves sufferers tired and poorly.

clue.text: Some say 20 is one putting up enclosure to confine Gulf state resident

indicators.note: to confine something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside another
in a down clue, putting up means the word is written upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: a cage is an enclosure for animals
someone from Oman, a state on the Persian Gulf, is an Omani

explanation.surface: Critics say the man at 20 is building a fence to hold someone from the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting up' reads the enclosure upwards as EGAC, and 'confine' holds the resident within. 20 across is the US president; 'Some say' marks the label as opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: His critics describe him as utterly self-obsessed, a person consumed by vanity and self-regard.

clue.text: A good time in Galway's disco, regularly visited with converted car

indicators.note: visited with joins the two pieces, the reworked car first
converted means changed into a different form, so the letters are rearranged
regularly takes every other letter of disco, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A night out at a disco in an Irish town, arriving by a car that has been modified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' turns CAR into CRA; 'regularly' takes I and C from dIsCo. The 's after Galway stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish word for fun, lively chat and entertainment, as found in a west of Ireland pub.

clue.text: Fantastic idea: put on Mozart's KV 365 for example

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly fanciful, so the letters are freely rearranged

explanation.surface: A concert planner thinks programming a particular Mozart work is a great plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fantastic' shuffles IDEA and PUT ON. KV 365 is Mozart's concerto for two keyboards, a piece for four hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A work for two keyboard players together is an instance of music for a pair of keyboardists.

clue.text: Sleep during sex — that's not appropriate

indicators.note: during means within a span of time, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: it is a long-standing euphemism for sex
a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: Nodding off in the middle of lovemaking is poor form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' marks the insertion; 'it' for sex is an old euphemism, as in Kipling's 'It' girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or ill-fitting, the same as being out of place.

clue.text: Raise tax on energy after Europeans acquire oil finally

indicators.note: after places the tax and energy pieces following the Europeans
in a down clue, on means placed above, so tax comes before energy
to acquire is to take something in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European, doubled for the plural

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of the word oil

parts.note: VAT is value added tax
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A call to put a levy on energy once Europe has secured its oil supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acquire' puts L, the end of oil, into EE, giving ELE.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate is to lift something higher, an ordinary verb synonym.

clue.text: Perhaps Rivera or Versace's private numbers gathered by AI

parts.note: a GI is a private soldier in the US army

indicators.note: something gathered by another is held inside it

parts.note: N is short for number, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A designer's secret phone numbers being collected by artificial intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: NN goes inside AI. The 's after Versace stands for 'is'. Gianni Rivera was an Italian footballer, Gianni Versace a fashion designer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both men share the same Italian first name, so it is an example given by two famous bearers.

clue.text: Leaderless Japan makes a decisive point

indicators.note: without its leader, the first letter is removed from the word

parts.note: Nippon is the Japanese name for Japan

explanation.surface: Japan without a captain still scores the winning point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaderless' drops the N from NIPPON.
explanation.definitionFit: In judo the winning score, a full point that ends the bout at once, has this Japanese name.

clue.text: Half of e-tailer about right to be included in decoration for president's achievement (certainly not 20's)

indicators.note: pieces included in another are placed inside it

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: half of takes the first three of the six letters of the online retailer's name

parts.note: Amazon is the best-known online retailer
ca is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A decoration awarded for a president's achievement, with a dig that it is not Trump's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be included in' puts the three pieces inside the British honour. The bracketed jibe works because the 20 across president spent years trying to repeal this health law.
explanation.definitionFit: The Affordable Care Act is the signature health reform of the 44th US president's time in office.

clue.text: Abandoned VAR in an ideal world?

indicators.note: abandoned means unrestrained and wild, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A football fan dreams of a world in which video refereeing has been dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' rearranges VAR IN AN. VAR is the video assistant referee used in football.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana is a state of perfect bliss, a heavenly place, hence the question mark for a looser sense.

clue.text: State agency arrests one involved in corruption

indicators.note: to arrest someone is to hold them, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up within, so a letter goes inside the word

parts.note: rot is decay or corruption
A means one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A government agency detains a person caught up in graft.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions nest: 'involved in' puts one inside corruption, and 'arrests' puts that result inside the agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Croatia is an independent country in the Balkans, so it is a sovereign nation.

clue.text: 20's immigration forces essentially banning Mexican people of old

parts.note: ICE is US Immigration and Customs Enforcement, the agency carrying out Trump's deportations

indicators.note: essentially points to the core, the central letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Trump's immigration agents are, in essence, keeping Mexicans out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes N from the centre of baNning and I from the centre of mexIcan.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were a tribe of ancient Britain, led by Boudicca in revolt against Rome.

clue.text: World Cup president endlessly wanting inside information

indicators.note: inside places the trimmed word within the other piece

parts.note: info is short for information

indicators.note: endlessly removes both end letters of the word wanting

explanation.surface: A football boss who keeps craving inside knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' strips W and G from wanting; 'inside' puts what is left within the short word for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Gianni Infantino heads FIFA, the body that runs football's world championship.

clue.text: I like eyes taking in new jab

indicators.note: taking in means holding something within, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: oculate means having eyes or eye-like spots

explanation.surface: Someone admires another's eyes as they're given a fresh injection.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside I + OCULATE, straight after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: To jab someone is to give them a vaccine injection, which is to immunise them.

clue.text: Farm building, old, like the ones accommodating half of us

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: accommodating means providing room for, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: those means the ones

indicators.note: half of takes the first of the two letters of us

explanation.surface: An old farm building, like the ones that house half of us.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes inside THOSE. An oast house is a kiln building for drying hops, typical of Kent in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Oast houses are found on hop farms, where the crop was dried, so they are agricultural buildings.

clue.text: Being surplus, Liverpool player leaves for one billion — that's more than enough

indicators.note: one piece leaves and is swapped for the other, a substitution

parts.note: redundance is the state of being surplus to need
Liverpool FC are nicknamed the Reds
A means one

explanation.surface: A footballer made surplus by Liverpool moves on for a huge fee, which seems plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: RED is replaced by A and B.
explanation.definitionFit: An abundance is a plentiful supply, an amount beyond what is needed.

clue.text: American car factory's beginning — of course every now and then — to produce optical device

parts.note: auto is American for a car

indicators.note: beginning picks out only the opening letter of factory
every now and then takes alternate letters, the first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: A US car plant begins making a lens, naturally, from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'every now and then' takes O, C, U, S from Of CoUrSe.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera's self-adjusting lens system, which sharpens the image without manual input.

clue.text: Dreadful times when sickness is around

indicators.note: a piece that is around another encloses it

parts.note: as means when
by means times, as in multiplying
mal is French for sickness, as in mal de mer

explanation.surface: Awful times when illness is everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is around' has when wrapping times; MAL is borrowed from French, as in mal de mer, seasickness.
explanation.definitionFit: Abysmal means appallingly bad, a synonym for terrible.

clue.text: Mostly faithful politician?

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word is kept

parts.note: true means faithful or loyal
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A question about whether a politician is largely loyal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' cuts TRUE to TRU. The whole clue is the definition, with a sardonic question mark about the man's fidelity.
explanation.definitionFit: The US president is a politician whose faithfulness, to spouses or allies, is often questioned.

clue.text: Those getting money and power turned up later

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word is written upwards, in reverse

parts.note: 'later!' is slang for goodbye, like 'see ya'

explanation.surface: People getting cash and influence who arrived late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses SEEYA to AYEES.
explanation.definitionFit: A payee is someone to whom a sum is paid, so these are recipients of cash.

clue.text: They could be frosty without the final bit of insulation

definitions.text: They could be frosty without the final bit of insulation

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the jumbled letters go outside the letter
could be suggests the letters might form something else when rearranged
the final bit picks the last letter of the word insulation

explanation.surface: Underwear may be chilly when it lacks a last layer of padding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' shuffles FROSTY to YFROTS, and 'without' puts it outside N. The whole clue describes men's briefs.
explanation.definitionFit: Men's briefs with an inverted letter-shaped front seam are thin and could leave the wearer cold.

clue.text: When taking part in basic skills regularly, A & E will become increasingly bloody

indicators.note: taking part in means joining within, so the letters go inside
regularly means at even intervals, one letter in each gap

parts.note: the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, are the basic skills

explanation.surface: A and E staff learn the basics as things become ever gorier.
explanation.walkthrough: A and E go into the gaps of RRR, one in each.
explanation.definitionFit: A rarer steak is less cooked, so it is redder and more blood-filled than another.

clue.text: Lovely sound of Grieg's Holberg for one

indicators.note: sound of means what is heard when a word is spoken

parts.note: Grieg's Holberg Suite is a well-known orchestral suite

explanation.surface: Praising the beautiful sound of a Grieg piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The word said is SUITE, which is pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet means charming or delightful, a common synonym in British speech.

clue.text: Cyclist's carrying headgear prior to a break

indicators.note: something carrying another holds it within

parts.note: Chris Hoy is a famous British Olympic track cyclist; the 's stands for 'is'

indicators.note: prior to means before, so the headgear comes before the letter A

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat or helmet

explanation.surface: A cyclist wears a helmet before a rest stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts helmet-plus-A inside the cyclist; Sir Chris Hoy is a British Olympic track champion. The 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday is a vacation, a period away from work, a pause from routine.

clue.text: Flat in Cleveland

indicators.note: in signals the letters sit within the place name

explanation.surface: An apartment in an Ohio city.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are inside cLEVELand.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat as an adjective means even or smooth, without bumps.

clue.text: Composer Bohuslav inspires each English writer

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so a piece goes inside

parts.note: Bohuslav Martinu was a Czech composer

explanation.surface: A Czech composer's music inspires each English writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspires', literally breathing in, puts the short form of each inside the composer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Harriet Martineau was a 19th-century English social theorist and author.

clue.text: One who backed Orban against a new candidate's extremist elements

parts.note: v is short for versus, against

indicators.note: the extreme elements of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A supporter of Hungary's leader opposing a fresh candidate's radicals.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer letters of candidate give C and E. JD Vance, the US vice-president, campaigned for Viktor Orban.
explanation.definitionFit: The US vice-president publicly endorsed Hungary's prime minister ahead of his election.

clue.text: Idiot inviting doctor to reverse most of crime stories in book

indicators.note: to reverse means the combined piece is read backwards
inviting someone in means holding them within

parts.note: a fool is an idiot

indicators.note: most of means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: theft is a crime
lies are untrue stories

explanation.surface: A fool lets a doctor in to undo most of the crime stories in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inviting' and 'to reverse' together give LORDOF, the idiot holding the doctor read backwards; 'most of' drops the last T of the crime.
explanation.definitionFit: William Golding's 1954 novel about schoolboys stranded on an island.
